topic: Particle Model of Matter and Pure Substances
key_concepts: All matter is made of tiny particles such as atoms, molecules, or ions.
Each pure substance has its own kind of particles.
Pure substances can be elements or compounds.
Elements are composed of only one type of atom.
Compounds are formed by chemically bonding two or more different elements.
Matter in solid, liquid, and gas states is made of particles.
Particles are always moving and have tiny spaces between them.
Heating particles makes them move faster; cooling makes them move slower.
Particles are attracted to each other.
Examples of elemental pure substances include copper, mercury, and helium.
Examples of compound pure substances include table salt, water, and carbon dioxide.
